+# Implementation Plan: Robust LLM JSON Parsing
+
+## Overview
+
+LLM responses sometimes include literal (unescaped) newline characters inside JSON string values. This is technically invalid JSON, but common enough in practice that `llm_read_json` must handle it gracefully. The fix adds a character-level repair pass that escapes only the newlines inside string values, leaving structural whitespace intact, and then re-attempts parsing.
+
+## Architecture Decisions
+
+- **Try-then-repair pattern** — attempt `json.loads` first (fast path); only invoke the repair pass on `JSONDecodeError` (avoids touching valid JSON).
+- **Character-level scanner** — walk the raw text tracking `in_string` / `escaped` state instead of regex, so nested escapes and quotes inside strings are handled correctly.
+- **Separate helper `_repair_json_newlines`** — keeps `llm_read_json` readable and the repair logic independently testable.
+- **Scope limited to `\n` / `\r`** — only the two characters that invalid JSON string literals most commonly contain; other malformed JSON is left to raise normally.
+
+## Dependency Graph
+
+```
+utils._repair_json_newlines   (new, no deps)
+        │
+utils.llm_read_json           (updated to call helper on error)
+        │
+tests.test_llm_read_json      (existing parametrized test, unchanged)

+```

+# Implementation Plan: Fix JSON parsing with embedded newlines
+
+## Overview
+
+LLMs sometimes return JSON where string values contain literal (unescaped) newline
+characters, which is invalid JSON. The `llm_read_json` helper in `paperqa/utils.py`
+was passing the raw text directly to `json.loads`, causing a `JSONDecodeError` in
+those cases. The fix adds a fallback that escapes embedded newlines (and carriage
+returns) inside quoted strings before retrying the parse.
+
+The issue is tracked in `ISSUE.md`. The fix and its regression test are the two
+units of work in this plan.
+
+## Architecture Decisions
+
+- **Try-then-fix pattern** — attempt `json.loads` first (no overhead for valid JSON),
+  then escape on `JSONDecodeError` and retry. This keeps the happy path fast and
+  avoids silently mangling already-valid JSON.
+- **Regex-based newline escaping** — `r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"'` matches each JSON string
+  token, honouring existing escape sequences, then replaces bare `\n`/`\r` with `\\n`/`\\r`.
+- **No new dependencies** — `re` is already imported in `utils.py`.
+
+## Task List
+
+### Phase 1: Bug Fix
+

+
+- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_paperqa.py::test_llm_read_json -v` — all 4 existing cases pass
+- [x] Manual smoke test with the exact JSON from `ISSUE.md` succeeds
+
+### Phase 2: Regression Test
+

+
+### Checkpoint: Complete
+
+- [ ] All tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_paperqa.py::test_llm_read_json -v`
+- [ ] New case covers the scenario from `ISSUE.md` (multi-line summary + numeric score)
+- [ ] Ready for review
+
+## Risks and Mitigations
+
+| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
+|------|--------|------------|
+| Regex misidentifies a `}` inside a string as the closing brace | Med | Existing text-trimming logic runs before the regex; strings can't span the outer `{}` boundary after trimming |
+| Escaped `\\n` in source text gets double-escaped | Low | `[^"\\]` in the pattern stops at `\`; the `\\.` arm consumes escape sequences whole, so `\\n` is never touched |
+
+## Open Questions
